statement: Public park documentation states that Tjukurpa includes knowledge of the location and care of rock holes, soaks, and other water sources, and that traditional practices maintain these water resources as part of caring for country.

sources.citation: Australian Government, Uluru–Kata Tjuta National Park World Heritage description, updated 16 Apr. 2026.
Uluru–Kata Tjuta National Park Plan of Management, public discussion of waterholes/soaks and traditional landscape management.

notes: The claim stays at the public level; it does not publish site-specific restricted information.
